justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modestly bullish baseline trajectory, starting near 166.2 for the one-day horizon and drifting upward to 170.0 over one month. The one-day estimate was anchored primarily by recent price momentum and short-term mean-reversion tendencies, assuming no major overnight catalysts. The one-week estimate of 167.5 incorporates a slight upward drift consistent with prevailing trend conditions while acknowledging that weekly fluctuations tend to partially offset short-term moves. The one-month estimate of 170.0 reflects a continuation of the broader trend, weighted by fundamental valuation anchors and the historical tendency for prices to gravitate gradually toward estimated fair value over medium-term horizons.

The confidence interval widths widen substantially as the horizon extends, which reflects the compounding of uncertainty over time. At one day, the 90% interval of roughly plus or minus 5.7 points captures normal intraday and overnight volatility, scheduled data releases, and liquidity conditions. By one week, the interval expands to cover a range of about 23 points, incorporating the possibility of earnings surprises, macroeconomic data, and shifts in market sentiment. At one month, the interval of roughly 45 points acknowledges that a full month introduces meaningful exposure to policy decisions, geopolitical developments, and broader risk-appetite swings that are difficult to anticipate with precision.

Several specific risks could push realized outcomes outside even these wider intervals. On the upside, an unexpected positive catalyst such as a stronger-than-anticipated earnings report, a dovish central bank pivot, or a resolution of a geopolitical risk premium could push prices well above 193 at the one-month horizon. On the downside, a sudden deterioration in macroeconomic data, a credit event, or an escalation in geopolitical tensions could drive prices below 148. Liquidity crises or flash-crash dynamics, though rare, represent tail risks that by definition fall outside the stated 90% confidence bounds and could produce extreme outcomes in either direction with very little warning.
